advisories.title: The ledger hedges on whether Claude v6 findings exist, while the Claude v6 verdict sits sealed in the same directory
advisories.subjectQuote: Claude v6 in-flight findings beyond those folded at v7 require a later successor if they exist.
advisories.detail: docs/coop/artifacts/sarif-projection-contract.v6.review-independent.claude2.json exists, is 15620 bytes and is frozen at 0444, and no claude2v6 pin appears in appliesFindingsOf. Meanwhile codexv6 is pinned, because honestyRepairsFromV6 folds CODEX-V6-B1 and CODEX-V6-S1. So the outstanding-items field carries an unresolved 'if they exist' about a lane whose verdict for that generation is present and frozen.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: Three reasons, and I want them on the record because I graded a superficially similar omission as SHOULD-FIX in the DR-101 lineage and this one is genuinely different. First, pinChainRule states that a successor pins the verdicts it folds and that earlier pins recover via basedOn.sha256; v13 folds nothing from Claude v6, so not pinning it is policy-consistent rather than anomalous. Second, there is no lane asymmetry to explain away: nine review files are unpinned on the same principle — codexv1 through codexv5, codexv9, claude2v2, claude2v3 and claude2v6 — so the Claude lane is not being singled out. Third, the hedge may simply be accurate: if that verdict carried no findings beyond what v7 folded, 'if they exist' is the right words. The prompt's read set does not include it and I did not open it, so I take no position on its contents — which is precisely why a hedge that one read would settle is worth flagging rather than faulting.
advisories.suggestedFix: Resolve the conditional. Either pin claude2v6 with its full roster as pinChainRule prescribes, or replace 'if they exist' with a determination once someone has read it.

verdictStatement: All four claimed repairs hold, and each answers the finding it names rather than gesturing at it. SARIFV11-A1 leaves notFolded only once the alias gap that justified withholding it is closed. ADV-SPC-V11-01 is recorded folded with correct attribution to the v12 rewrite, in a better-chosen list than the one I proposed. The CODEX-V<n>-* alias is documented, and I tested the consequence rather than the wording: SARIFV6-B1, a blocker-grade finding that resolved to no column at v12, now resolves. The post-commit qualifier is grounded against the exact committed-Run boundary field I raised it against. Beyond the repairs, everything I could think to attack held. The roster covers all thirteen changed paths including a scope qualifier the bytes respect; the substantive contract is byte-identical to v12 across fifteen keys; the row quote and the 26 carried lines are byte-exact against live sources; the folded and not-folded sets are disjoint and every recorded finding resolves to exactly one column; no D9 code, exit, RunId, Finding or artifact-ref recipe is minted, which I confirmed at the golden rather than the disclaimer; G17 is refused everywhere it appears; and reMeasurementAtV13 is live at the current HEAD rather than merely reconciled. My strongest line of attack was the artifact's own pinChainRule, which twelve folded findings appear to violate until its recovery clause is read; it holds. One advisory remains, on a hedge about whether Claude v6 findings exist, and it does not block. This is the first version in this lineage I can accept, and the thing that changed is that the ledger is now checkable by script instead of by hand.

coordinatorNote: ACCEPT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-122 stays OPEN at file 08 line 304; nothing here marks it SATISFIED, authorizes implementation, resurrects G17, mints a D9 or DR-006 recipe, or creates anything under D-096 (A). I rejected v12, so the basis for the change should be visible: all four v12 findings from my lane and both from Codex are repaired, each verified from live bytes rather than from the repair roster, and no earlier repair regressed. Two things I want to flag for the record rather than as findings. First, my one advisory concerns an unpinned Claude v6 verdict, and I have deliberately graded it lower than the superficially similar omission I called a SHOULD-FIX in the DR-101 lineage; the difference is that this artifact states a pinChainRule that makes not pinning an unfolded verdict policy-consistent, and nine review files across both lanes are unpinned on that same principle, so there is no lane asymmetry here. Resolving the 'if they exist' conditional is still worth one read by someone whose scope includes that file — mine did not. Second, the durable improvement this round is not any single repair but that the ledger became machine-checkable: the documented alias means a sweep for unaccounted findings now returns nothing rather than four false positives, which is what let me verify the whole thirty-plus finding roster instead of spot-checking it. That property is worth preserving in any successor.
